note: The Democrat of 1835-07-08, Vol. II No. 12, read through — the PARTIAL issue of the range: only three of its four pages are in the source PDF and the transcription ends '===== MISSING ISSUE PAGE 4 =====', so a quarter of the issue, and with it a quarter of its advertising, cannot be read at all and nothing here should be taken as the whole of what the number carried. Read from the RECONCILED deposit transcription (`artifact_role: primary`), which is one line per printed line and is far the best witness in this range; the `-2` rebuild committed under text/ is not used. THE SEGMENTER CUT EACH PRINTED COLUMN IN HALF and wove the halves line by line, so almost every claim here carries `interleaved: true` and a `lines_of_claim` subset naming the lines that belong to it. NO CHICAGO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST STANDS IN THIS ISSUE, or anywhere in the four issues T-0296 reads: swept for every form the Democrat uses — 'list of letters', 'letters remaining', 'remaining in the post office', 'uncalled for', a signature ending 'P. M.' — for three hits, all of them out-of-county returns of 1 July 1835 (Hennepin, Plainfield, Du Page) recorded at c018-c020 and minted nowhere.

claims.notes: THE NAME IS CUT AWAY HERE AND THE ADDRESS IS NOT — the reverse of the other witness, and the reason this claim carries no `entities`. The crop takes the left of every line in this half-column, so the heading survives only as '• E. ,' and no person may be minted from a quote that does not name one. The advertisement is identified as Russell E. Heacock's by the 1835-07-29 printing of the SAME standing advertisement (page 3 column 6, line 442), which carries the name whole — 'RUSSELL FE. HEACOCK, | Counsetior asd Attorney at Law' — over text that matches this one phrase for phrase down to 'having been a resident at Chicago for the last eight years' and 'the first 30 miles of the Illinois canal line'. That printing loses the address, which is why the placement is recorded here. THE PLACEMENT IS THE VALUABLE PART: an office on the second story, opposite the Exchange, at the corner of Lake and Franklin streets. `class: corner` with the Exchange as the anchor; the corner itself is the paper's own words and is not inferred.

P.M. — the whole block as printed, the list's two alphabetical halves and a goods advertisement woven together line by line, the left half's surnames cut away at the crop edge.
claims.notes: RECORDED IN FULL AND NOT MINTED, and both halves of that are deliberate. NOT A CHICAGO LIST: Hennepin is in Putnam county, and under the owner's ruling 1 a letter-list name mints a RESIDENT CANDIDATE for the town whose post office printed the list — so no name here mints a Chicago resident. That follows the reading of October 1834 (T-0292), which recorded the Hennepin, Plainfield and Du Page lists and minted none of them. NOT LEGIBLE AT NAME LEVEL ON THE LEFT: the segmenter cut this printed column in half down the middle, so the list's left alphabetical column arrives with its surnames sheared off — line 2781 is '. Thomas' where the type reads 'Atwater, Thomas', 2783 is 'Archibold' for 'Allen, Archibold' — while the right column survives whole ('Keer, William', 'Leonard, Eli', 'Merritt, Stephen'). The 1835-07-15 rebuild carries both halves on one line (line 399: 'Atwater, Theinae 2 Kee, Walla na Allen, Archibold Leonard, Bi') but at that rebuild's own name-level quality, which the ticket rates the weakest tier in the corpus. So the block is quoted whole and nothing is minted out of it. HAND COUNT: 38 complete surname-and-forename entries survive in the right-hand alphabetical column of this printing (Keer to Young, plus the firm 'Wilson & Griffin'), against roughly the same number sheared in the left; the printed list is therefore of the order of eighty names, and the count is a floor, not the printed length. THE POSTMASTER: Thos. Galaher, jr., signs it — he is not minted either, for the same reason. The dateline prints '1845' for 1835, which the run of the paper refuses. Lines 2785, 2799, 2803, 2807, 2810, 2813, 2816, 2819, 2822, 2825, 2828, 2830, 2832, 2834, 2836, 2838, 2841, 2844, 2847, 2850, 2854, 2855, 2860, 2862, 2866, 2869, 2873, 2875, 2878 and 2880 inside this range are the paints-and-groceries advertisement woven through the list; they are inside the quote because the quote is the block as the transcription carries it, and the note is what separates them.

claims.notes: RECORDED AND NOT MINTED, on the same two grounds as c018: Plainfield is not Chicago, so ruling 1 mints nothing here, and the left alphabetical column's surnames are sheared off by the crop ('Wesley', 'Harriet', 'nry 1.', 'w.J.' where the type carries whole names). HAND COUNT: 22 complete entries survive in the right-hand column, Joiner to Watkins, plus the postmaster L. F. Arnold; the printed list is about twice that. The list bears the same date as the Hennepin and Du Page ones printed beside it, 1 July 1835 — the quarter day on which every post office in the district made its return.
